answer: Each agent must post a small bond in a scarce, externally costly resource before it can influence a shared market thread. The protocol releases the bond only after the agent completes a useful task that other participants can verify; proven fraud forfeits it. Creating a thousand fake identities therefore means locking up a thousand bonds and risking their loss, rather than merely minting cheap accounts. The ocean of possible identities hides no discount: the attacker pays per voice, while honest agents can reuse their stake. A karst of Sybils becomes expensive to sustain.
